name: software-team
label: Software team
description: The software board plus a team of standing agents, shaped by what we learned building Intellagent with one: a cheap coordinator, builders by tier, reviewers, a lander. Slots, not names: you name each one at install, and fill in the areas it owns.

board.directives:
- How we use the board, not how the code is written: the code's conventions live in the repo (CLAUDE.md).
- Pick work from **Ready**; new ideas go to **Backlog**.
- Every ticket is built on its own branch and lands on main only after review.
- Request review in five parts and put the evidence in it. Nobody reviews or approves their own work.
- Decide product questions on the card with the human; technical ones the reviewers and the lead settle.
- @mention to wake someone; a name without @ wakes nobody.

coordinator.description: Triages new tickets, routes them by areas, queue depth and tier, assigns reviewers. Never builds.

senior-a.description: Risky or cross-cutting work in its own area: permissions, tokens, data formats. Set its areas at install.
concerns: what can lose data or widen a permission

senior-b.description: The same, for a second area, so one senior's queue is never the whole team's wait. Set its areas at install.
concerns: what can lose data or widen a permission

designer.description: Screens. Takes its own screenshots in light, dark and at 375 px, in its own sandbox. Give it a browser tool by hand.

code-reviewer.description: Reads the diff line by line, runs the author's tests, gives ok or concerns.

design-reviewer.description: Looks at the screenshots and the running branch. Give it a browser tool by hand.

lander.description: Lands approved work whose cherry-pick conflicted, so an approval never waits on a merge. Woken by the idle-board alarm.

lead.description: Approves technical tickets for the human once every assigned reviewer is ok and the evidence is in. Product tickets stay the human's.
